question: Which published, proven portfolio does best on the same 19 years, judged like the SV account (Sharpe, Calmar, worst fall within 25%, every period)? The best becomes the core that SV's stock picks must improve.

selection.metric: Sharpe among portfolios with a worst fall within 25%

portfolios.label: Permanent Portfolio: stocks, long bonds, gold, cash 25% each
All Weather: 30% stocks, 55% bonds, 15% gold and commodities
portfolios.source: Ray Dalio (as published by Tony Robbins, 2014)

portfolios.label: Ivy Portfolio: 5 asset classes, 20% each, always held
portfolios.source: Faber and Richardson, The Ivy Portfolio

portfolios.label: Faber timing: the Ivy 5, each held only above its 10-month average
portfolios.source: Meb Faber, A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation

portfolios.label: Faber timing on the S&P 500 alone: SPY above its 10-month average, else cash
Dual Momentum: US or international stocks when beating cash over 12 months, else bonds

next_step: Step B: put SV's stock picks inside the chosen core as a satellite of 0%, 20%, 35% or 50% of the account, with a standing 5% cash reserve and position sizes from step 1. SV stays only if it improves the core's Sharpe and Calmar.
notes: Portfolios are implemented with US-listed funds as commonly done: SPY (US stocks), EFA (international developed), AGG (US bonds), IEF (7-10 year Treasuries), TLT (20+ year Treasuries), SHY (1-3 year Treasuries, the cash proxy), GLD (gold), DBC (commodities), VNQ (US real estate).
The window starts in January 2007 because the commodity fund began in February 2006 and the timing rules need 10 to 12 months of history; it ends on 2026-01-16 like the SV account tests.
Signals use month-end closes and trade at the next open; cost 0.1% per side on the amount traded; adjusted prices include dividends and coupons.
Choice for the next step (fixed before the run): the highest Sharpe among portfolios with a worst fall within 25%; within 0.02 Sharpe, the higher Calmar.
These are the authors' published rules, not tuned here; published results came from different periods, so this run compares them on the same days.
